The petitioners - accused Nos.2 and 3 are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 109 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, alleging that, the defacto complainant is the wife of the accused No.1, and the accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-law.

2. The allegation against the accused Nos.2 and 3 is that, they instigated the accused No.1 to subject the defacto complainant to cruelty both physically and mentally, and also bring money from the parental home.
The accused No.1 and the defacto complainant were residing at matrimonial home at Bengaluru.
On 30.6.2021, the accused No.1 forcibly sent the defacto complainant to parental home at Kalburagai and demanded to bring a sum of Rs.5 lakh from the parental home.
On 9.12.2021, all the accused came to the parental home, picked up a quarrel, abused her in filthy language and threatened that they would do away her life.
The learned Magistrate, after accepting the charge sheet, took the cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1237 Taking exception of the same, the accused Nos.2 and 3 are before this Court.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners - accused Nos.2 and 3 and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
4.
The charge sheet material indicates that, the accused No.1 and the defacto complainant were residing at Bengaluru.

On 30.6.2021, the accused No.1 forcibly sent the defacto complainant to the Devappa Gadad And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148834851/
2 parental home demanding to bring money.

sentences.text:
On 9.12.2021, all the accused came to the parental home,
abused her in filthy language and also threatened with dire consequence.

The specific allegation demanding money and abusing her in filthy language is as against the accused No.1, and except the general and omnibus allegation, there is no allegation against the accused Nos.2 and 3 as to how and in what manner subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both physically and mentally.

The last of the events alleging that, the accused Nos.2 and 3 along with accused No.1 subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both physically and mentally were on 9.12.2021 and 14.5.2021 respectively,
and the FIR was lodged on 11.7.2022 without offering any plausible explanation.

5. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599 has held that,
the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus NC: 2023:KHC-K:1237 allegations, unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, there is no specific allegation against accused No.2 and 3, who are parents-in-law, except general and omnibus allegations to constitute the above offences.
6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao [(2008) 15 SCC 582]

entities.text: State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao [(2008) 15 SCC 582]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
has held as follows:
"30.
Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
7.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, the delay in filing the FIR should be explained, and in the absence of such explanation, the FIR lodged becomes an afterthought.
In the present case, the FIR was lodged against accused Nos.2 and 3 after two months without offering any plausible explanation.
Hence, the registration of FIR lacks plausible reasons for the delay and is not permissible in law.

In the absence of any specific allegations as against the accused Nos.2 and 3, the charge sheet laid against them only on the basis of omnibus NC: 2023:KHC-K:1237 and general allegation is without any substance.
Hence, the continuation of criminal proceeding against the accused Nos.2 and 3 will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in CC No.20634/2022 pending on the file of the learned I Additional JMFC at Kalaburagi, insofar as it relates to petitioners - accused Nos.2 and 3 is hereby quashed.
